Clapper omitted Snowden revelations, Congress neglecting their responsibility
During Former National Intelligence Director James Clapper's tenure as a public official, he consistently refused to respond to any Questions from Congress regarding the surveillance of U.S. persons. The omission in his testimony of the degree to which the NSA spied domestically, as leaked by whistleblower Edward Snowden, is, according to legal strategist Jeffrey Folkerts, “yet another indicator that Congress is failing the American people by not adhering to its Constitutional duties regarding foreign invasions of privacy.”
